Source: KRONOS Parameter Guide (official Korg documentation)
  URL: https://cdn.korg.com/us/support/download/files/74a6c3cb0399c4d733d5730cd4c4e7f8.pdf
       (filename: KRONOS_Param_Guide_E11.pdf)
  Fetched: 2026-08-03
  Sections: page 18 ("Program P0: Play" > "0-1a: Program Select" > "Category"),
            page 811 ("Global mode" > "Global P3: Category Name")

Why this was pulled: while researching the CMB/PRG physical-bank-placement
problem (see STATE.md's EXPLORATION section), the project owner asked what's
known about Category -- a per-Program/Combi attribute used for browsing sounds
by type (Keyboard, Bass, Strings, etc.), independent of which bank/number a
sound lives at. This turns out to be structurally the SAME kind of problem as
Bank type (HD-1/EXi): a small per-record index whose *meaning* depends on a
per-unit-customizable name table stored in Global settings (GLB1) -- directly
relevant to "what has to be checked/reassigned when moving a Program or Combi
between two different datasets."

--- Excerpt (page 18, Program mode) ---

Category [00...18, Name]
All programs are classified into one of eighteen categories, such as
Keyboard, Organ, Strings, etc. Each of these categories may also have up to
eight sub-categories. Selecting by Category lets you search for a specific
type of sound (like an electric bass, for example), without concern for what
Banks the sounds are stored in.

[...]

All: All programs in the category will be shown. Choose this when you don't
need to use sub-categories.
0...7: The programs will be shown by sub-category.

You can assign a category to a Program in the "Write Program" dialog.

--- Excerpt (page 811, Global mode) ---

Global P3: Category Name

Programs, Combinations, and KARMA GEs are organized into categories and
sub-categories. Categories make it easy to find a particular type of sound,
such as keyboards, bass, or drums, or a specific type of KARMA GE, such as
arpeggios or gated patterns. Each main category also has up to 8
sub-categories, for finer degrees of organization.

Anywhere that you can select Programs, Combinations, or KARMA GEs by bank and
number, you can also select them from the category pop-up.

When shipped from the factory, there are 16 preset Program and Combination
categories, with 2 more left open for your use (initially named User16 and
User17). There are also 12 preset KARMA GE categories.

On these pages, you can:
- Change the names of any of the categories and sub-categories, including
  BOTH the factory and user categories
- Add sub-categories to the factory categories (up to the limit of 8)

You can assign a Program or Combination to a category and sub-category
during the Write process.

To save changes to category names, you'll need to write the Global
settings, using the menu command "Write Global Setting."

3-1: Program Category
3-1a: Main Category
  Main Category 00...17
  Main Category Edit [(Text Editor)] -- rename any of the eighteen Main
  Categories for Programs (up to 24 characters each).
3-1b: Sub Category
  Main Category select [00...17]
  Sub Category 00...07
  Sub Category Edit [(Text Editor)] -- rename any of the eight Sub
  Categories within the selected Main Category.

3-2: Combi Category
3-3: KARMA Category
  These pages let you assign the main category and sub-category names to
  Combinations and KARMA -- same mechanism as 3-1 above, but a SEPARATE
  table from the Program one. Note: you can rename existing KARMA
  categories, but you CANNOT reassign which category a KARMA GE belongs to
  (unlike Programs/Combis, which CAN be reassigned to a different category
  during Write).

--- What this confirms for this project ---

- Category is a real, per-Program AND per-Combi attribute (two SEPARATE
  18-main x 8-sub category tables, not shared) -- not yet located in either
  record's raw bytes; not mentioned anywhere in the Synthify PCG File
  Structures spreadsheet or DaBlick's reverse-engineering notes already in
  this project, so the byte offset is genuinely unexplored, same status as
  the rest of GLB1 (see docs/README.md's chunk tree, "GLB1 -- NOT explored").
- The category NAME table (all 18 names + up to 8 sub-names each, for BOTH
  the Program table and the separate Combi table) is stored in Global
  settings and fully user-renameable -- including the 16 "factory" names,
  not just the 2 open User slots. This table almost certainly lives inside
  `GLB1`.
- Direct implication for cross-dataset Program/Combi moves: a record's
  Category is (presumably) just a small integer index, whose displayed
  *meaning* depends on a per-unit-customizable name table -- structurally
  identical to the Bank-type problem (see the other docs/external files).
  Two datasets with differently-renamed categories could show a moved
  Program's category as a misleading label in the destination. Confirms the
  project owner's instinct that this may need explicit user confirmation/
  reassignment when moving Programs/Combis between datasets whose category
  tables don't match -- not solved or built, just confirmed as a real
  question worth tracking (see STATE.md's EXPLORATION section).
- Two concrete pieces of future reverse-engineering this points at, neither
  started: (1) locate Category/Sub-Category's byte offset within a Program
  record and (separately) a Combi record -- needs the same purpose-built
  test file methodology already used for Font size/Transpose/Combi Timbre
  refs; (2) parse GLB1 itself, at minimum enough to extract the category
  name tables -- GLB1 has never been touched at all so far.
